title: Big orders, your team and a 90-day expansion plan

say: Big orders, your team, and a 90-day expansion plan.
This is the video for module three of Factory and Workshop Setup.
A tidy, safe workshop helps you win bigger buyers. But only honest capacity keeps them. Never promise more than your workshop can produce.

say: For example, a hotel group asks Hauwa for 400 bags in 18 working days. She makes 22 bags a day, and regular customers take 15. So she has 7 spare a day.

panel.heading: Hauwa's 400-bag order in 18 days
items: Spare capacity: 22 - 15 = 7 bags a day
Over 18 days: 7 x 18 = 126 bags
Shortfall: 400 - 126 = 274 bags
Offer options: split, add a machine, or partner

say: Check all five before you say yes. Materials are bought before the buyer pays, so agree a deposit in writing.
Get the sample approved in writing and keep it as the standard. Confirm any transfer in your own banking app, not from a screenshot or text alert, before you release goods.

panel.heading: Before you accept a big order
items: Spare capacity covers it

say: On the first day, walk a new person through the whole flow. Show the exit, extinguisher, first aid kit, main switch and chemical store. Then train each task in four steps. Tell: explain the standard and the safety points.

panel.heading: Teach any task in four steps
items: Tell: the task, the standard, the safety points
Show: do it slowly while they watch
Do together: they do it, you correct
Check and sign off: alone, to standard

say: A skills matrix scores each person on each task, from 0, not trained, to 3, can train others. Hauwa saw that only she could cut and inspect. If she travels, both stages stop. So she is cross-training a machinist and the apprentice.

panel.heading: Three tools for a small team

cards.d: People down the side, tasks across the top, scored 0 to 3. Find tasks only one person can do.
Each zone has a named owner who checks daily that it is stocked, clean and safe.
Every machine has a named person for routine care, following the manual.

say: Expand at the bottleneck. For Hauwa that is sewing, so she prices a third machine. Capacity would rise to 792 bags a month, but she does not assume she will sell them all. From buyer conversations she expects about 60 extra bags at first.

card.title: Is a third machine worth it?

say: The machine, table and socket cost about 500,000 naira. The extra bags bring 180,000 naira a month. A third machinist and power cost 85,000.

card.title: Is a third machine worth it?

say: That leaves 95,000 naira extra profit a month. Payback is one-time cost divided by extra monthly profit: about 5.3 months.

card.title: Is a third machine worth it?

say: On cautious sales, the machine pays for itself in about five to six months.

But if she sells only 30 extra bags, profit drops to 5,000 naira a month, and payback becomes 100 months. That is why she waits for confirmed orders and a deposit before buying. Never borrow against a full-capacity forecast.
Write your plan in four phases. Confirm demand before buying. Then install, with a safe socket and a place that keeps the walkway clear.

panel.heading: A 90-day expansion plan
items: Days 1-30: confirm demand, get quotes
Days 31-60: buy, install, wire
Days 61-75: hire and train
Days 76-90: run, measure, review

say: Leave time to hire and train before you rely on the new capacity, and update your risk assessment. At day 90, review output, sales, running costs and incidents.

say: To remember. Check capacity, cash and quality before you say yes. Cross-train so no task depends on one person. Expand at the bottleneck, work out payback on cautious sales, and test it against a bad case.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Check capacity, cash and quality before yes
Train in four steps; cross-train key tasks
Expand at the bottleneck
Payback = one-time cost / extra monthly profit
Test the plan against a bad case
